newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds firm on U.S. rates, Congress vote.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds firm on U.S. rates, Congress vote.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose strongly Wednesday as buyers emerged on the back of stable U.S. rates and the Argentina Congress approval of a law allowing the central government to keep all the revenues from a planned fuel tax hike.
"The market put in a very strong performance," said a trader at a large foreign bank.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.50 to 118.50, while Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 6/8 to 84.
Traders said the decision by the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee Tuesday to leave rates steady supported the market as investors sought higher yields. Surging U.S. Treasuries helped.
The Congressional approval, though anticipated, of a bill letting the government collect all the anticipated $1.6 billion of revenues from a fuel tax hike also helped the bond market.
Failure to approve the bill could have forced the central government to share the revenue with provincial governments.

In the coming two sessions, players warned, the market could see slim activity because of a 36-hour general strike protesting the government's economic policies. Reduced public transport may mean some players stay away from work.
And, "if there are any large disturbance during the strike, the market could be concerned," said the trader.
In the money markets, call money rates were unchanged at 5.50 percent.
